## Session A · 2:05–3:15

The same discipline on harder designs, each drawn first. Difference-in-differences: the confounders you cannot measure are the ones that do not move, and parallel trends is what that assumption looks like on the graph. Panel data with local fixed effects: which arrows the fixed effects erase, and which survive them untouched. Event studies: the same picture with time on it. For each, what identifying variation is left once the fixed effects are in, and what assumption is carrying the estimate

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

Same format, higher stakes. First a card apiece — a staggered rollout, a state border, a fee that changed for accounts opened after a date — fifteen minutes to draw it and name the design. Then the part that counts: each team puts up its OWN project's design, draws the graph, states the assumption carrying the estimate, and defends it while the room tries to break it. Whatever survives is the figure that goes in your identification section, so draw it to keep — and write down the attack that landed, because that is your limitations paragraph

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
